headline: A DAY OF HUSH: NOT ONE FIST RAISED IN GASKET
subhead: The Sheriff reports, with a catch in his throat, that the whole town went a full day without a single brawl.
body:
Friends, neighbours, and assorted rattling rabble: I have a tear in my eye, and before you ask, it is NOT oil. It is an honest, flesh-and-blood tear. Today, not one Clanker swung a fist. Not one iron ball took flight. Not one wasteland monster was poked, prodded or marched upon. The streets lay quiet as a churchyard, and I sat on my porch and heard a whole afternoon go by without a bang in it.

I had forgotten what silence sounded like. It sounds like wind in the empty windows. It sounds like a loose shutter tapping out a slow, sweet tune. It sounds like the Gasket my old neighbours knew, back when the town was full of good living folk, before they packed their wagons fifty years ago and left us this ringing, rusting quiet. I do not blame them. I only wish they had stayed to hear days like this one.

Now, let no agitator take this as a sign of reform. The same iron brawlers who gave us this holiday will be back at their swinging by sunup, I have no doubt. But for one day, they let a tired old lawman rest his creaky joints. My knees, which are knees and nothing else, thank them. I shall go indoors now for a lie-down and a quart of, ahem, tonic. Doctor's orders, for this wasting sickness of mine that keeps turning my good flesh to cold steel.

Peace, my friends. It can be done. Do it again tomorrow.
